title: F77 default — variables starting I–N are INTEGER, all others REAL (no IMPLICIT NONE)
sourceContent:
SUBROUTINE COMPUTE_TOTAL(A, B, TOTAL)
C     NO IMPLICIT NONE. By F77 default:
C       A, B, TOTAL -> REAL (first letter R, A, T -- A and T are
C                            non-I-to-N -> REAL; R likewise)
C       I, J, K, L, M, N -> INTEGER
C       NEW_TOTAL -> INTEGER (starts with N)
      INTEGER I
      DO I = 1, 10
         TOTAL = TOTAL + A + B
C        Watch out: if a typo wrote NEW_TOTAL by accident, the
C        compiler would silently allocate it as INTEGER.
      END DO
      END
notes: I–N implicit typing is the single biggest source of accidental type bugs in legacy F77. A modern Java/C# rewrite enforces declared types, which often FIXES bugs the legacy code carried for decades. The spec must flag the implicit rule so the rewrite's type choices are deliberate.
